rules: For every future study, use the original RCT PDF and Mandros extraction Excel as the only required study inputs; a manual Excel benchmark is not required.
Inventory the entire PDF before extraction.
Apply standards/optimal_extraction_prompt_v1.md and standards/clinical_trial_statistics_v1.json automatically for every future trial; the user does not need to request the skill.
Build the expected-finding inventory from the PDF independently of the Mandros Excel before declaring completeness.
Classify each source finding as continuous, binary, count/rate, ordinal, time-to-event, repeated-measures or another explicitly supported type before interpreting its numerical components.
Preserve exact trial-specific arm, endpoint, instrument, subgroup and analysis-population terminology; normalized labels may supplement but never replace the source term.

Link every extracted number to its study, arm/comparator, outcome definition, metric, aggregation, timepoint, subgroup, population, statistical type and source locator; isolated numbers remain incomplete.
One row is one independently interpretable observation.
Keep value, unit, operator, dispersion, timepoint, arm and population scope in separate fields.

Represent less-than, equal-to and greater-than as separate columns. In Excel exports, write the literal symbols <, = and > in their own cells before the related numeric value and unit; leave non-applicable operator cells blank. Represent bounded ranges with minimum and maximum fields instead of a combined operator string.
Use blank/null for unreported values; never encode missingness as NA, zero or a dash.
Every arm reference must resolve to one canonical arm record.
Do not convert randomized N, analyzed N, visit counts or denominators into one another.
Store n_randomized, n_baseline and n_analyzed as separate population fields and never infer one from another without an explicit derivation rule.
Extract inclusion and exclusion criteria separately, including subgroup-specific thresholds.
Do not fabricate baseline values when the article does not report them.
Do not create outcome records for unavailable supplementary material; inventory only the files actually supplied and extract only source-reported values.
Separate efficacy, safety and adherence/process measures.
Use sample_proportion when a reported proportion is calculated from the trial sample.
Keep analyzed sample size, event count, denominator and proportion in separate fields; do not substitute randomized N for a per-protocol denominator.
Preserve exact table and text values. Do not silently digitize figure-only values; flag them as figure-only unless a documented digitization workflow is used.
Record all published timepoints and classify within-arm versus between-group estimates.

Store each p-value once in Statistical Tests, with its operator separate from its numeric value. Link a between-arm test to both arm-specific outcome rows using one comparison_id; do not duplicate the p-value in both arm rows or attach it to one arm only.
Require page-level provenance and an explicit verification state.
Give each analytical record an explicit estimate_type, source_status, canonical record identifier and include_in_meta_analysis decision.
Give each analytical record an independent_study_id, estimand_family, meta_analysis_eligibility value and a human-readable eligibility reason.
Use only READY, REQUIRES_REVIEW or NOT_POOLABLE for record-level meta_analysis_eligibility; include_in_meta_analysis is true only for READY records.
Do not pool different estimands such as baseline means, final means, changes from baseline, proportions and hazard ratios as though they were interchangeable.
Do not invent variance. When SD, SE, CI or another valid uncertainty measure is absent, preserve the reported result and require review or mark it not poolable.
Do not double-count the same finding when it appears in the abstract, prose, table or figure; retain one canonical observation and multiple provenance locations.
Treat one randomized trial as one independent study; multiple outcomes, timepoints and subgroups do not become independent studies.
Preserve reported statistical methods and p-values separately from arm-level observations and effect estimates.
Represent published internal contradictions with conflict_id and a machine-readable source-conflict record; do not silently choose or recalculate a replacement value.
Reject fabricated, wrong-arm, wrong-value, wrong-timepoint and unresolved duplicate records.
Run an independent second pass before a workbook can be called verified.

Validate every numerical record as a complete source identity tuple: study, outcome, arm or comparison, timepoint, analysis population, analyzed N or denominator, statistical type, value, unit and source locator. A page-level numeric match alone is insufficient.
Apply a blocking primary-endpoint gate before scientific validation. The source-defined timepoint, metric, arm, population, uncertainty type, value and unit must all match.
Do not classify rescue-therapy thresholds, visit schedules, discontinuation conditions, follow-up rules or analysis-population definitions as eligibility criteria.
A generic normalization pass without an independent PDF inventory may export a draft but must not claim scientific validation.
When a source statement, project rule or requested change conflicts with another authoritative item, preserve both, do not silently edit scientific content, and require human adjudication.
PRISMA applies to systematic-review reporting; CONSORT/RoB 2/ICH E9 apply to trial extraction and appraisal.
